The page was re-captured for this fragment on 2026-10-26T15:19:00Z (local_data/country-research-q3-china-operators-p3/cscec-ulanqab-1024.html, 95,189 bytes) and its SHA-256 is byte-identical (cd0b51c2...d0f8), so the earlier retrieval time and metadata are kept unchanged to resolve to the same evidence record.
sources.summary: CSCEC (China State Construction Engineering Corporation) group news item published 24 October 2026 (发布日期), compiled from submissions by its subsidiaries, describing CSCEC's data-centre and energy construction work in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia. Under the heading '世纪互联乌兰察布零碳智算中心A1楼-机电总包工程' (VNET Ulanqab Zero-Carbon Intelligent Computing Center building A1 - mechanical and electrical general contract) it says that, in the Ulanqab high-tech zone, China Construction Second Engineering Bureau has carried out the installation of low-voltage, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, interior fit-out and roof steel-structure specialty works for building A1, and that once the project is built it will advance the construction of the Ulanqab zero-carbon intelligent computing center. The section's production manager (a named CSCEC employee, not reproduced here) describes the work as one building's mechanical and electrical installation, including pipework, equipment and commissioning tests that determine whether the centre can run safely and stably. A separate section of the same item reports that the Eighth Engineering Bureau's Phase 1 A2 mechanical and electrical general contract (the existing Atlas project) has entered final acceptance. Other sections cover UCloud building D, Envision phases 1 and 3, Huawei Phase 3 DC5/Phase 4 DC4, Kuaishou stage 2 and energy projects; none of these is used here. The item gives no capacity, completion date, commissioning date or customer for A1.
sources.date_semantics: Published 24 October 2026. A contractor's own report of mechanical, electrical and fit-out installation work on building A1 under its M&E general contract, with the building described as not yet completed ('项目建成后'). It is read as an observation that A1 is in its mechanical, electrical and fit-out stage as of the publication date. No start day, completion day, commissioning or operation is stated or inferred.
sources.status_statement_excerpt: 中建二局为世纪互联乌兰察布零碳智算中心A1楼进行了弱电、暖通、给排水、电气、精装修及屋顶钢结构等专业工程的安装。项目建成后将推动乌兰察布零碳智算中心建设
sources.firsthand_participant: China Construction Second Engineering Bureau (中建二局), the A1 M&E general contractor, is a CSCEC subsidiary; the item is CSCEC's own publication.

sources.title: Stafford County Board of Supervisors: minutes of the regular meeting of 18 August 2026 (item 19, Potomac Church Tech Center proffer amendment, ordinance O26-25)
sources.summary: Item 19 considered a request to amend the proffered conditions on tax map parcel 39-71A (project known as Potomac Church Tech Center proffer amendment; proposed ordinance O26-25). The Director of Planning and Zoning told the Board that the amendment concerned potable-water use for the Potomac Church Data Center project, that the site lies on the east side of Old Potomac Church Road across from its intersection with South Campus Boulevard, and that the approved site development plan shows two proposed data center buildings: 'On the left was the first building that was now complete and occupied.' Under the existing proffers the first building may use potable water for cooling until reclaimed-water (reuse) lines reach the site, and the second building cannot be occupied until those lines are built; the amendment allows occupancy of the second building before the reuse system is complete, keeps the 217,000 gallons-per-day potable-water cap for both buildings for no more than 24 months after the second building's occupancy permit, requires bonds for the reuse upgrades and adds a USD 10 million transportation contribution due before that occupancy. The applicant's counsel said the site's Tier 2 generators had been approved in March 2025. The Planning Commission had recommended approval 6-0 on 13 May 2026, and the Board approved O26-25 by 4 votes to 2 with one member absent. The applicant's counsel said the construction process had started (without stating its scope) and gave July 2028 as the expected finish of the second building; the Director relayed the applicant's estimate that occupancy of the second shell would otherwise slip from April 2027 to 2029.
sources.date_semantics: Minutes of the meeting held on 18 August 2026 (statement on PDF page 52, counsel's remarks on page 53, vote on page 61), published on the county's CivicClerk portal on 13 October 2026 (publishOn 2026-10-13T16:51Z). The Director's statement that the first building was complete and occupied is used as an observation that Building 1 was complete and occupied on 18 August 2026; the minutes give no completion, occupancy-permit or service-start date, so none is inferred. The second building's April 2027 and July 2028 dates are forecasts and are not used; its construction stage is not established.
sources.pages_reviewed: whole document (81 pages); item 19 on PDF pages 52-61
sources.personal_data_note: Names of residents who spoke and of individual officials are not copied; officials are identified by title.
